acceptance: Root cause identified for each mismatching query with an executed sqlite3 vs DuckDB comparison on the same data.
Fix lands in the right layer (loader, fork generator, or benchmark) with a regression test, or the query is a registered SQLite skip with reason.
The published bundle is flagged with a known_defects id if its recorded rows were wrong, per results-data provenance policy.
description: Found by the published-results audit (history://AffectedResults; noted in results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md by #3398). In the published SQLite ClickBench SF1 bundle (…6eb94fe6) about 25 of 43 queries return row counts that differ from all 9 other engines, e.g. Q8 1 row vs 20, Q11-Q15 0 rows vs 9-10. The SQL changes since v0.4.1 touch only Q19 and Q43, so a rerun alone will not fix it. Likely causes to rule in or out: loading (empty strings vs NULL, type affinity of text/numeric columns), translation, or the SQLite reference data.
